logline: In a world transformed by an app that rings when someone within ten metres has romantic feelings for you, a high school girl at the centre of a love triangle must decide what the alarm's silence or ring actually means about herself.

renewal.note: Two-season run concluded March 12, 2021. Netflix confirmed no further seasons. Adapted from Chon Kye-young's webtoon; noted as one of the first Korean dramas confirmed for Netflix global distribution.

bollymeter.basis: Rotten Tomatoes Season 1 score of 65% from 4 critics reflects mixed reception; the social-commentary dimension around app-mediated feeling earned genuine praise while the flat lead performances drew criticism. The show ranked 6th among most-watched K-dramas globally on Netflix in 2021, confirming real audience reach.

seasons.review_body: Love Alarm landed on Netflix in August 2019 as one of the first Korean dramas the platform confirmed for global streaming. Season 1 drew attention for its premise, an app that rings when someone nearby has romantic feelings for you, and the strongest material leans into social commentary on digital validation, surveillance of emotion, and the coercive pull of quantified feeling. Rotten Tomatoes lists a 65% score across four reviews. The central love triangle between Kim Jo-jo, the earnest Hye-yeong, and the more magnetic Sun-oh drives consistent engagement, with Song Kang’s performance as Sun-oh adding extra pull. The 8-episode first season delivers its premise with momentum, even as the lead performances can feel uneven. Netflix Top 10 data from 2021 places the show 6th among most watched Korean dramas on the platform that year.

episode_reviews.title: Your Heart Is Safe Now
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the app's social logic efficiently and places Jo-jo immediately at the intersection of two very different boys. The world-building is brisk - the show is less interested in explaining the technology than in exploring what it does to people's behaviour - and the romantic tension is established without melodramatic scaffolding.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Jo-jo's first encounter with the app ringing in an unexpected direction - the premise's central tension is activated within the first episode.

bollymeter.basis: The Review Geek scored it 5/10; critical consensus on Season 2 flagged a compressed arc and a resolution that many viewers found abrupt after the Season 1 premise setup. The shorter six-episode count underserved the emotional payoff.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived in March 2021 with six episodes, a notably shorter run than Season 1. The season advances the story by two years and introduces a shield feature that blocks the app's signal, a device that reads as more dramatically intriguing in concept than in execution. The ending provides closure for those invested in the love triangle, though a time skip softens the impact of the characters' emotional arcs and the season does not quite match Season 1's tonal confidence.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 trades the premise-driven energy of Season 1 for a truncated resolution arc; the emotional stakes are present but the shorter episode count leaves less room to earn them.
